note.en: What you see: The probe lies in the oesophagus directly behind the left atrium, so the atria sit at the top of the sector and the ventricles open below toward the apex. All four chambers appear in one plane with the mitral valve on the left of the image and the tricuspid valve on the right. The interatrial septum and the interventricular septum run across the middle of the image and the coronary sinus may show as a small round vessel in the posterior groove. Because the beam travels only a short distance through blood before reaching the valves, leaflet detail is crisp and near field gain should be kept low to avoid clutter behind the left atrium.

label.en: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, right ventricle cavity, right atrium

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, right ventricle cavity, right atrium cavity, anterior and posterior leaflets of the mitral valve, anterior and septal leaflets of the tricuspid valve, interatrial septum, interventricular septum, coronary sinus, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

steps.en: What you see: The probe lies in the oesophagus directly behind the left atrium, so the atria sit at the top of the sector and the ventricles open below toward the apex. All four chambers appear in one plane with the mitral valve on the left of the image and the tricuspid valve on the right. The interatrial septum and the interventricular septum run across the middle of the image and the coronary sinus may show as a small round vessel in the posterior groove. Because the beam travels only a short distance through blood before reaching the valves, leaflet detail is crisp and near field gain should be kept low to avoid clutter behind the left atrium.

Landmarks to confirm: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, right ventricle cavity, right atrium cavity, anterior and posterior leaflets of the mitral valve, anterior and septal leaflets of the tricuspid valve, interatrial septum, interventricular septum, coronary sinus, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

Common mistakes and correction: Foreshortened left ventricle with a rounded apex that hides the true apex: advance or withdraw slowly with slight anteflexion until the apex opens and the ventricle looks longest. Probe too deep so the stomach crowds the image: withdraw until the sector clears. Probe too shallow so the aortic valve dominates: advance a little. Too much gain in the near field hiding the atrial septum: lower near gain before judging septal defects.

Normal values with units: Probe depth about 30 cm from the incisors at the mid oesophageal station. Multiplane angle 0 degrees. In health all four chambers contract symmetrically and no fluid separates the pericardial layers. Left ventricular ejection fraction 52 percent or above in men and 54 percent or above in women marks the lower reference limit.

Pitfalls: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so thickened mitral leaflets with restricted opening in a young breathless patient should prompt careful Doppler assessment rather than dismissal as artefact. A prominent Eustachian ridge in the right atrium can mimic a mass. Known oesophageal disease, unstable cervical spine injury and severe dysphagia are reasons to defer the study and seek senior advice.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: After topical anaesthesia of the throat and sedation per local protocol, advance the probe gently in the midline with the tip straight to about 30 cm from the incisors. Set the multiplane angle to 0 degrees. Anteflex slightly until all four chambers open in one plane. Centre the mitral valve, then set depth so the left ventricular apex sits just inside the bottom of the sector. If only the atria show, advance a little. If the aortic valve dominates the image, withdraw a little until the four chambers balance.

remember.en: Recognise foreshortening and correct it before judging function

q.en: Where should the probe tip sit for the mid oesophageal four chamber view?

why.en: The mid oesophageal station lies about 30 cm from the incisors, directly behind the left atrium.

q.en: Which multiplane angle gives the four chamber plane from the mid oesophagus?

why.en: The four chamber plane is the zero degree baseline from which the two chamber and long axis planes rotate.

q.en: The left ventricle looks short with a rounded apex. What is the correct response?

o.en: Advance or withdraw slowly until the apex opens and the ventricle looks longest
Increase far gain to brighten the apex

why.en: A short rounded apex means foreshortening, so the probe position must change until the true apex opens, not the gain.

q.en: A young breathless patient shows thickened mitral leaflets with restricted opening. What next?

o.en: Dismiss it as artefact of the near field
Assess the leaflets carefully with Doppler because rheumatic disease is common in India
Withdraw the probe and abandon the study
Increase output power to burn through the thickening

why.en: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so thickened restricted leaflets deserve careful Doppler assessment.
